blocks.text: Mission Court-Ordered Sales: streets and boundaries

items.t: A 2025 BC Supreme Court case naming the City of Mission, Herar v. Mission (City), 2025 BCSC 1553, was filed in the Abbotsford Registry and heard in Abbotsford.
The Abbotsford Supreme Court registry is at 32375 Veterans Way, Abbotsford; that courthouse opened to the public on January 18, 2021, and Supreme Court trials began there February 1, 2021.

blocks.text: Mission Court-Ordered Sales: the housing stock

items.t: Any mortgaged Mission property can be the subject of this process: Rule 21-7 of the Supreme Court Civil Rules covers a proceeding for foreclosure of the equitable right to redeem mortgaged property, or for redemption, and it must be started by petition.

blocks.text: Mission Court-Ordered Sales: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The BC court-ordered-sale process starts with a petition: Rule 21-7 requires a foreclosure proceeding to be started by petition in the Supreme Court of British Columbia.

The petitioner must serve an information sheet with the petition: Rule 21-7 (4.1) requires a petitioner who serves a foreclosure petition to include the informational notice for foreclosure proceedings in Form 125.

The first court order is the Order Nisi, which fixes the amount owing and the redemption period; in 1048977 B.C. Ltd. v. Aviva, 2025 BCSC 1532, the court granted an order nisi with a six-month redemption period and later extended that period by two months.

A sale is not final until the court approves it, and foreclosure hearings follow Practice Direction 66 (PD-66); BC Courts announced on March 31, 2026 that PD-66 was updated so foreclosure applications other than approval-of-sale applications may be heard in virtual chambers.

blocks.text: Mission Court-Ordered Sales: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Mission's tax sale runs on a fixed date: the City holds a public auction at 10:00 a.m. on the last Monday in September each year in Council Chambers at City Hall, and bidders must register by 9:45 a.m.
Tax sale questions go to a named City line: the City lists Tax Sale Inquiries at 604-820-3717 on its tax sale page.

blocks.text: Mission Court-Ordered Sales: development and new projects

items.t: Foreclosure hearing practice changed in 2026: BC Courts' March 31, 2026 announcement records the PD-66 update allowing foreclosure applications, except approval of sale, to be scheduled in virtual chambers.

blocks.text: Mission Court-Ordered Sales: costs and taxes

items.t: Mission property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, and a 10% penalty was added to outstanding current balances on July 3, 2026.
Unpaid Mission taxes draw interest before any tax sale: the City states that on January 1, 2026, outstanding 2025 taxes moved to arrears with an interest charge of 7.45%.

Mission's 2026 flat-rate utilities total $1,892.28 for a single-family home that receives the services: water $641.76, sanitary sewer $786.60, garbage $166.92, and recycling and compostables $297.00, charged on the annual tax notice.
The same Mission home with a secondary dwelling pays $3,207.60 in 2026 flat-rate utilities.
Mission also levies additional taxes for diking, on top of the municipal rate.

blocks.text: Mission Court-Ordered Sales: risks and due diligence

items.t: A tax sale purchase is not final for a year: the City states the original owner has one year after a tax sale to pay the taxes and buy the property back, which is the tax sale redemption right.
Tax sale properties are sold without any City warranty: the City states all property sales at tax sale are "as is" without warrant or guarantee by the City of Mission.

faq.q: Where is a foreclosure of a Mission home actually heard?
faq.a: Not in Mission, because Mission has no Supreme Court registry.

faq.q: How long does the owner get to pay out the mortgage and stop the sale?
faq.a: The Order Nisi sets that redemption period, and the court controls its length.

faq.q: Can I check whether a Mission property is already in foreclosure?
faq.a: Yes, through Court Services Online, the Province's court records service.

faq.q: Is a City of Mission tax sale the same thing as a foreclosure?
faq.a: No, they are different processes run by different bodies. A tax sale is the City selling a property whose taxes have not been paid for three years, under sections 645 to 672 of the Local Government Act. A foreclosure is a lender's Supreme Court proceeding under Rule 21-7, started by petition, with an Order Nisi and a court-set redemption period.
